city_center.name: Downtown Missoula / Clark Fork riverfront
city_center.landmark: the Clark Fork River through downtown, Mount Sentinel with the 'M' above the University of Montana; the 'hub of five valleys' at the convergence of five mountain ranges
city_center.notes: Missoula sits along the Clark Fork River near its confluence with the Bitterroot and Blackfoot, the 'hub of five valleys'; the Clark Fork River Market and the Missoula Farmers Market (north Higgins Avenue) anchor summer-fall weekends. Montana Snowbowl is 12 miles northwest. sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missoula,_Montana; clarkforkmarket.com; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montana_Snowbowl.

cultural_notes: Missoula sits along the Clark Fork River near its confluence with the Bitterroot and Blackfoot rivers, at the convergence of five mountain ranges -- 'the hub of five valleys' (source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missoula,_Montana)

wild Montana huckleberries are a signature regional food, found at the Clark Fork River Market alongside local produce, bread, honey and wool goods (source: bluemountainbb.com Missoula farmers markets; clarkforkmarket.com; destinationmissoula.org)

downtown holds a documented late-1800s to 1940 commercial-architecture historic district -- brick storefronts from the railroad-and-timber era (source: NRHP Historic Resources in Missoula 1864-1940, nps.gov)
the Bitterroot Salish are the region's Indigenous people; any tribal reference stays consent-gated -- no fabricated endorsement (INFERRED framing; verify + honor sovereignty)
